title: That Tallow Balm That Smells Like a Pear Jelly Bean
body:
Okay so I just got home and my hands were wrecked. Like, dry and tight and just gross. I was doing dishes earlier and I guess the soap here is just the worst, it’s the cheap stuff from the big plastic bottle, you know the one. Anyway. I saw this little jar on my counter. The Whipped Tallow Balm. The pear one. I got it a few weeks ago because my skin was just being a jerk all winter and I was desperate. Beef fat for your face sounded… I don’t know. Weird. But I was out of my usual stuff and this Etsy shop kept popping up and the pictures looked nice. So I got it.

I opened the jar. It’s white and whipped, looks like frosting. And the smell hit me. It’s not a fancy perfume smell. It’s not “notes of” whatever. It just smells like a green pear jelly bean. The good kind. Not the fake candy pear, but like, if you bit into a really crisp, cold pear and also maybe you’re near a flower? But not a flower-flower. I can’t describe it. It’s just nice. Light. It doesn’t smell like beef. At all. Which, you know, was my first worry with a natural pear tallow balm. It just smells clean and a little sweet and fresh. Like spring. Which is good because it’s finally spring and my skin is still confused about it.

I scooped a little out. It’s cold from sitting on the counter. The texture is… thick but not greasy? It melts as soon as you rub your fingers together. It just disappears. I put it on my hands and my knuckles, which were all red and angry. It soaked in fast. My hands just felt… normal. Not slippery. Not sticky. Just not tight anymore. I sat there for a second just smelling my hands. It’s that kind of scent. Makes the whole thing feel less like a chore and more like a little treat. My cat jumped up and sniffed my hand and then gave me a look like “what is that” and then walked away. Cats, man.

## How I Ended Up Putting Beef Fat on My Face

Look, I need to back up. The whole beef tallow skincare thing. I heard about it online. People were going nuts for it. I thought it was a fad. Or gross. I pictured like, a tub of lard. But then I read that tallow, like from grass-fed cows, is actually really close to the oils our own skin makes. Our sebum. So it makes sense that your skin would know what to do with it. It’s not some weird chemical it has to figure out. It’s just… food. For your face. This stuff is whipped beef tallow balm from France, made from grass-fed suet. They whip it so it’s this fluffy, light texture. It’s not what you picture.

I was using this expensive cream before. The one in the fancy glass jar that costs like a week of groceries. It smelled like a department store. It did nothing. My skin would be okay for an hour and then it’d be tight again. I felt ripped off. So when I saw this scented tallow balm, I figured, what’s the worst that could happen? It’s cheaper than the fancy junk. If it’s terrible, I’ll just use it on my elbows or something.

## What This Pear Tallow Balm Actually Does

So I tried it. Not just on my hands. I used it at night, after I washed my face. My routine is a mess, I just use a basic cleanser and then sometimes I remember moisturizer. I’d been skipping it because everything felt heavy. This pear balm, I put a tiny bit between my palms, let it melt, and then just press it into my skin. Don’t rub it around like crazy, just press. It sinks in. It doesn’t sit on top. My face felt… calm. Not shiny. Not greasy. Just hydrated. The scent is so subtle and gentle, it’s just there for a minute and then it’s gone, but it makes the whole process feel sophisticated in a really simple way. Like you’re doing something nice for yourself without trying too hard.

I started using it on everything. My cuticles. My elbows, which are always rough. I put a tiny dab on my lips before bed. Woke up and they weren’t chapped. That never happens. I keep the jar by my bed now. It’s become the thing I do last before I turn the light off. A little ritual. The pear smell is just part of it. It’s light and fresh and fruity, and it doesn’t clash with anything. It’s just pleasant. It makes me look forward to using it, which is weird to say about a moisturizer. But it’s true. I find myself opening the jar sometimes just to smell it. It’s that kind of good.

## My Skin After a Few Weeks of This Stuff

I don’t want to sound like an infomercial. But my skin is different. The dry patches on my cheeks? Gone. The winter damage on my hands? Healing. It’s not a miracle, it’s just… consistent. It works every time. I used it after I got a little sun last weekend, just on my shoulders, and it soothed it right away. It’s deeply hydrating without being heavy. I’m on my second jar now. I got one for my mom too because she was complaining about her knuckles cracking. She texted me last week like “what is this magic butter?” She calls it that. Magic butter.

The best part is I don’t think about it anymore. It’s just what I use. My skin isn’t a problem I’m constantly trying to solve. It’s just… my skin. It’s fine. It’s better than fine. It’s healthy. I caught my reflection in the microwave door the other day—you know, that weird dark reflection—and I was like, huh. My face looks calm. Not red. Not angry. Just calm. And I swear it’s because of this tallow balm. I stopped using all the other potions. This is the only thing that’s ever actually mimicked my skin’s own sebum well enough to make a real difference.

## Would I Buy This Scented Tallow Balm Again?

Yeah. I already did. Like I said, second jar. I’ll probably get another when this one runs low. It’s become a staple. I even took it on a trip last month, in my carry-on. It’s solid, so no spills. The scent is just… it’s the right choice. It’s not overpowering. It’s not fake. It’s just a gentle, sophisticated sweetness that makes the whole experience enjoyable. If you’re curious about natural pear skincare, or tallow in general, this is a really good place to start. It’s from this little Etsy shop, just a person making it, which I like. Feels more real than something from a big factory.

Anyway. My neck hurts from looking down at my phone. I should go to bed. But first, I’m gonna put a little more of that pear tallow balm on my hands. Because why not.

## Quick Questions I Get Asked

**Is beef tallow good for your face?**
Yeah, surprisingly. It sounds wild, but it’s really similar to the oils our skin already makes. So it absorbs deep and doesn’t just sit on top clogging stuff up. It’s like giving your skin food it recognizes.

**Does tallow balm clog pores?**
Not for me, and I can get clogged pores easy. This stuff sinks in. It’s not pore-clogging because it’s so similar to our own sebum—your skin knows how to use it. It’s the weird synthetic stuff that usually causes problems.

**What does the pear tallow balm smell like?**
It’s hard to pin down. It’s not a strong perfume. It’s like a crisp, fresh pear with something clean behind it. Not candy-sweet. Just light, fruity, and really pleasant. It’s the main reason using it feels like a little treat.

If your skin’s being difficult, or you’re just tired of products that don’t work, this might be worth a shot. It’s just a simple thing that works. I don’t know what else to say.
